briefFull: The objective of the scheme is to promote the adoption of Spice Slicing Machines to mechanize post-harvest processing, improve operational efficiency, and enhance the quality of spices for export.
details:
Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – Spice Slicing Machines (Nos.) is implemented by the Spices Board, India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
The objective of the scheme is to promote the adoption of Spice Slicing Machines to mechanize post-harvest processing, improve operational efficiency, and enhance the quality of spices for export.
The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits:
- 50 % of cost of unit, subject to a maximum of ₹ 9000/- per unit for General Category and 75% subject to maximum of ₹13,000/- per unit for NE/SC/ST & 90% Spice Producer's Groups in Identified Clusters subject to maximum of ₹ 16,000/-
- Spices growers having a land holding size of 0.40 ha to 8 ha
- Assistance for groups/FPOs will be as in QGBG
eligibility:
1.All spice growing States and regions in India/UT.
2. Designated Officials will conduct final inspection and recommend the eligible cases.
howToApply:
[Online]
**Registration**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website.
Step 2: Click on the “[Register” ](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/citizenRegistration.html)option on the homepage.
Step 3: Fill out the registration form by entering Full Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, Password, selecting State, and Captcha.
Step 4: Review all details carefully and submit the registration form.
Step 5: An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number or email; enter the OTP and click “Verify.”
Step 6: Registration will be completed successfully, and a confirmation message will be displayed or sent via email.
**Login**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the ServicesPlus website and click on [“Login.”](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/loginWindow.do)
Step 2: Enter your Email ID, Password, and Captcha.
Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name.
Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form.
Step 5: Submit the application.
documentsRequired:
a) Aadhaar Card
b) Current year land tax receipt / chitta adangal/Parcha copy / Possession certificate indicating the total area /NoC for NE
c) Bank Pass book
d) CR /ACR if applicable
e) Invoice and payment documents towards purchase from valid manufacturer of the equipment/device empaneled by Spices Board

faqs.q: What is the objective of the Spice Slicing Machines scheme?
faqs.a: The scheme aims to promote the use of Spice Slicing Machines to mechanize post-harvest processing and improve the quality of spices for export.
The scheme is implemented by the Spices Board, India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.

faqs.q: Who can apply for this scheme?
faqs.a: Eligible spice growers with a land holding of 0.40 hectares to 8 hectares can apply. Eligible groups and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) may also apply as per the scheme guidelines.

faqs.q: Which areas are covered under the scheme?
faqs.a: The scheme is available in all spice-growing States, Union Territories, and regions of India.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available for General Category applicants?
faqs.a: General Category applicants are eligible for 50% of the unit cost, subject to a maximum of ₹9,000 per unit.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available for NE/SC/ST beneficiaries?
faqs.a: Eligible applicants from North Eastern States, SC, and ST categories can receive 75% of the unit cost, subject to a maximum of ₹13,000 per unit.

faqs.q: What assistance is available for Spice Producer Groups in identified clusters?
faqs.a: Eligible Spice Producer Groups (SPGs) in identified clusters can receive 90% of the unit cost, subject to a maximum of ₹16,000 per unit.
Yes. Applicants must submit the invoice and payment documents for the machine purchased from a Spices Board-empanelled manufacturer.

faqs.q: Is proof of land ownership or possession required?
faqs.a: Yes. Applicants must submit valid land documents or a No Objection Certificate (NOC), wherever applicable.

faqs.q: Can Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) or groups apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Eligible groups and FPOs can avail assistance as per the applicable group assistance guidelines.
